title: Section 3(a) - Definition of Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani Drug
section_title: Section 3(a) - Definition of Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani Drug
authority: Ministry of AYUSH & Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO)
publisher: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare / Ministry of AYUSH
content: Section 3(a) defines 'Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani drug' to include all medicines intended for internal or external use for or in the diagnosis, treatment, mitigation or prevention of disease or disorder in human beings or animals, and manufactured exclusively in accordance with the formulae described in the authoritative books of Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani Tibb systems of medicine specified in the First Schedule.

title: Section 33A to 33N - Chapter IV-A: Provisions Relating to ASU Drugs
section_title: Section 33A to 33N - Chapter IV-A: Provisions Relating to ASU Drugs
authority: Ministry of AYUSH & Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO)
publisher: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare / Ministry of AYUSH
content: Chapter IV-A of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 governs the manufacture, sale, and distribution of Ayurvedic, Siddha, and Unani drugs. It establishes the Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani Drugs Technical Advisory Board (ASUDTAB), the Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani Drugs Consultative Committee (ASUDCC), standards of identity and purity, Government Analysts, and Licensing Authorities.

title: The First Schedule - Authoritative Books of Ayurveda System
section_title: The First Schedule - Authoritative Books of Ayurveda System
authority: Ministry of AYUSH & Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO)
publisher: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare / Ministry of AYUSH
content: The First Schedule lists the 54 authoritative classical Ayurvedic treatises recognized for statutory licensing under Section 3(a): Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridaya, Ashtanga Samgraha, Sharangadhara Samhita, Bhavaprakasha, Madhava Nidana, Bhaishajya Ratnavali, Sahasrayogam, Rasa Tarangini, Ayurvedic Formulary of India (AFI Part I-III), and Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India (API).

title: Rule 158B(1) - Classical Ayurvedic Medicine Licensing
authority: Ministry of AYUSH & Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO)
publisher: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare / Ministry of AYUSH
content: Under Rule 158B(1) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945, a manufacturing license on Form 25-D for Classical Ayurvedic formulations requires proof that the recipe, ingredients, and method of preparation are verbatim described in an authoritative text listed in the First Schedule. No safety or efficacy trials are required if manufactured strictly per classical texts under Schedule T GMP.

title: Rule 158B(2) - Patent or Proprietary (P&P) Ayurvedic Medicine Licensing
section_title: Rule 158B(2) - Patent or Proprietary (P&P) Ayurvedic Medicine Licensing
authority: Ministry of AYUSH & Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO)
publisher: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare / Ministry of AYUSH
content: Rule 158B(2) mandates that for Patent or Proprietary (P&P) Ayurvedic medicines containing ingredients from First Schedule texts but with novel proportions or delivery forms: (a) If claiming textual indications, published safety data or pilot clinical trial data must be submitted; (b) If using novel purified extracts or modified fractions, full acute/sub-acute toxicity studies and clinical efficacy trials are required.

title: Rule 161 - Labeling, Packing and Limit of Alcohol in ASU Drugs
section_title: Rule 161 - Labeling, Packing and Limit of Alcohol in ASU Drugs
authority: Ministry of AYUSH & Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO)
publisher: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare / Ministry of AYUSH
content: Rule 161 specifies mandatory labeling requirements: (a) Clear declaration of 'Ayurvedic Proprietary Medicine' or First Schedule textual name; (b) Full qualitative list of ingredients with official Sanskrit/Latin names and quantities; (c) Manufacturing license number, batch number, date of manufacture, date of expiry; (d) Storage conditions; (e) If containing Schedule E(1) poisonous plants, bold warning: 'Caution: To be taken under medical supervision'.

title: Schedule T - Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for ASU Drugs
section_title: Schedule T - Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for ASU Drugs
authority: Ministry of AYUSH & Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO)
publisher: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare / Ministry of AYUSH
content: Schedule T lays down factory requirements for hygienic manufacturing of Ayurvedic drugs: location and surroundings, building structure, water supply, raw material warehouse, dedicated extraction area, batch manufacturing records (BMR), quality control testing laboratory, retained samples room, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).

title: Schedule E(1) - List of Poisonous Botanical Substances
section_title: Schedule E(1) - List of Poisonous Botanical Substances
authority: Ministry of AYUSH & Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO)
publisher: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare / Ministry of AYUSH
content: Schedule E(1) lists poisonous botanical substances requiring Shodhana (purification) and statutory medical supervision warnings: Aconitum heterophyllum (Vatsanabha/Ativisha), Datura metel (Dhattura), Strychnos nux-vomica (Kupilu), Semecarpus anacardium (Bhallataka), Cannabis sativa (Bhanga), Croton tiglium (Jayapala), and Gloriosa superba (Langali).
